coverage.row: Scenario 1-2: guest writes tree in one isolate, snapshot, restore in fresh isolate before guest code, identical listing (ino aside)
Scenario 3: consumer realm restores the bytes into MemoryFs; a realm-built tree restores in an isolate
Scenario 4: truncated/flipped/bad CRC/version/template/duplicate/non-canonical/under-file/unknown kind/over maxBytes refused by name, FS unchanged, both realms
I1 round trip: kind, bytes, readdirSync order, statSync (ino aside) for any name rifty's FS holds (<=16 383 units, amend 2026-11-22), both realms both directions; gaps named in compat
I2 version + template in blob; other version/template refused by name; later rifty reads earlier versions
I3 hostile bytes: named, no blob text, target unchanged, linear, maxBytes before allocation, nothing outside target
I4 limits: snapshot over maxBytes before allocation, restore over maxBytes before read, restore only before guest code, snapshot after guest code guest-authored
I5 same tree same bytes; snapshot changes nothing
I6 cost published for small and template scale, both realms; template scale each direction <= 2 s, peak isolate memory <= 2 x S + 64 MiB (M3 Pro)
